label: <DEL> step of long sequences starting with w/0/o/a/i
explanation: Very sparse (about 0.03% of steps) and fires only at the delimiter step (100% of mass), which is also where recall_idx==0 starts. Rate rises steeply with L: L=9 holds 73% of mass and L=8 holds 18%; it never fires for L=3 and almost never for L<=5. It is strongly gated by the first original token (the token output at this step): w (41% of mass, 23x lift), 0 (21%), o, a and i. A second token of w/u/y/t/0/i raises precision further (to about 0.15-0.23), and top examples look like w w ..., 0 u ..., 0 w .... It never fires in the original or copy phases. The predicate gets most of the mass (dev mass recall 0.82) but precision is only about 0.05: most long sequences starting with these tokens do not cross the threshold, so the firing seems to depend on a distributed hidden-state condition that the token-level variables only partly capture. Magnitude is larger for L=9 and first token w.
